# Scientific closure requirements

These requirements govern every numbered retained-research stage. They are user requirements, not optional recommendations.

- Start from the exact verified integrated parent. Record both workflow SHA and checked-out scientific SHA.
- Commit prospective preregistration before new scientific execution. Disclose all already-known exploratory findings; never relabel them preregistered after the fact.
- Freeze mathematical objects, primary objectives, diagnostic objectives, full enumeration domain, competing outcomes, resource rules and stopping rules.
- Use algorithmically independent production and verification. Reconstruct the entire canonical universe and require exact identity equality, not supplied-record validation or count checks alone.
- Include substantive rejecting controls: missing, duplicated and substituted records; wrong values; invalid states/moves; false provenance/coverage. Preserve genuine RED evidence and failed runs.
- Provide typed mathematical arguments and distinguish general proofs, bounded evidence and unresolved propositions. No finite no-counterexample result is a universal theorem.
- Run the complete inherited foundational stack with pinned dependencies on GitHub. Inspect exact logs.
- Upload source, complete scientific certificates, logs, metadata and checksums as execution artifacts. Freshly reproduce deterministic scientific bytes in the publication job.
- Commit durable scientific evidence and verified manifests to GitHub; inspect downloaded artifact digests, not just upload success.
- Mark PR ready only after review, scientific verification and publication closure. Merge the verified head and audit the actual merge SHA, including replay, manifests, coverage and inherited stack.
- Never use CLOSED/CERTIFIED for a stage before the post-merge audit passes. Report every missing requirement explicitly.
- For barriers, primary B1, Binf and Bs are three INDEPENDENT scalar minima. LEX_BARRIER is a separate diagnostic. Their bounds need not be jointly attained by one path.
- Time is pruning / ordered recoverability update. Combinatorial barriers do not imply physical energy, action, metric, gravity or fundamental time.

Future agents must continue the complete closure chain within the user's authorized scope; recording a plan or contract does not resolve a requested run.

# v16.26 — Proof ledger

## P1 locality
Removing a leaf c from one view changes only membership of c. Since c is a child of v and has no retained descendants in that view, only A_i(v)=Ch_U(v) intersect Y_i changes. All other child-incidence families are identical.

## P2 atomic bound
Let t=tau_v(before). v16.25 monotonicity gives tau_v(after)>=t. If any t-view cover survives, equality holds. Otherwise choose an old t-view cover S. The deleted c was essential to S. Same-union admissibility supplies another final view j containing c. Then S union {j} covers all children after deletion, so tau_v(after)<=t+1. Thus tau_v(after) is t or t+1.

## P3 exact trigger
By definition tau remains t iff at least one old minimum t-cover remains a cover after deletion. Therefore it rises iff every old minimum cover is destroyed.

## P4 global increment
Only tau_v can change and it changes by at most one. Since h=max(1,max tau), delta h is 0 or 1. It equals one exactly when the changed local value exceeds the previous global maximum.

## P5 atomic factorization
For a same-union endpoint refinement Z_i subset Y_i, repeatedly remove a leaf of Y_i\Z_i. Prefix closure is preserved. Every removed node belongs to the common final union, so some Z_j contains it and hence it remains in that view throughout. Thus each atomic step preserves the union. Finite repetition reaches Z.

## P6 path independence of total
For any atomic factorization V_0 -> ... -> V_m, sum_k (h(V_k)-h(V_{k-1})) = h(V_m)-h(V_0) by telescoping. P4 makes each summand 0 or 1. The locations of ones need not be canonical; the total is.

No fundamental time, response operator, or geometry enters.

# Attempt to derive the pruning-record interaction

Date: 2026-10-11. Immutable inspected parent: 7c4d7ec35845295d2fe578e4ce57ebe93bbeb589.

## Approved physical objective and concrete candidate

The preceding pruning-record result proves a protected conditional record under same-union pruning of indexed views. The approved next objective is to obtain the interaction from an inherited mechanism, with a retained accessible output, rather than adopt deletion-only evolution because it makes the example work.

The candidate tested here is the inherited canonical ancestral retraction: choose a retained prefix-closed set Z in a supplied lineage tree T, and apply the SAME retraction to every indexed retained view. This is the most literal way to try to obtain the prior view-pruning interaction from common lineage pruning. The retained set Z itself is still supplied; the obstruction below holds even after granting arbitrary selection of Z, including source-dependent selection. It is a structural failure of this proposed connection, not a complaint that an actual outcome has not been selected.

The source trace also checks whether the existing event-sufficient quantum operation or extensive source pushforward repairs this particular connection. Neither is dismissed as mathematically invalid. Their input types and supplied premises are recorded separately.

## 1. Uniform ancestral pruning leaves surviving incidence unchanged

Let T be a finite rooted prefix tree, with a finite nonempty fixed index set P. Let (Y_i) be root-containing prefix-closed views with union T, and let S_v={i:v in Y_i} be the equivalent native nested supports. Let Z subset T be nonempty, root-containing and prefix closed. The inherited map r_Z:T->Z sends each vertex to its longest retained ancestor.

Define the proposed uniformly pruned views by direct image:

    Y'_i = r_Z(Y_i).

**Identity.** For every i,

    r_Z(Y_i) = Y_i intersect Z.

Proof. If y belongs to Y_i, every ancestor of y belongs to Y_i. In particular r_Z(y) belongs to both Y_i and Z. This proves one inclusion. Conversely, if z belongs to Y_i intersect Z, r_Z(z)=z, so z belongs to the image. QED.

The pruned views are prefix closed and have union Z. At every surviving vertex v in Z,

    S'_v = {i:v in Y'_i} = {i:v in Y_i} = S_v.

Thus uniform ancestral pruning removes whole vertices from the common carrier but changes no indexed support at a surviving named vertex. The statement is about support membership, not about local hitting numbers on a changed child set, extensive amounts, or a newly chosen decoder. Those other quantities can change.

This gives an exact realization test. A P-indexed target cover (W_i) of a retained prefix tree Z is obtainable by the proposed uniform operation iff W_i=Y_i intersect Z for every i, equivalently iff its support at each surviving vertex is the original S_v. Necessity is the identity; sufficiency follows by applying r_Z. No numerical search or normalization theorem is used, and no general originality claim is made for this elementary retraction identity.

If the output union must remain the original T, then Z=T. The uniform operation is then the identity on every view. In particular it cannot perform any nontrivial same-union incidence deletion from the preceding result.

The same conclusion survives any finite composition of uniform prefix prunings. Each surviving named vertex keeps its initial support; equivalently the composed ancestral retraction is the direct retraction to the final retained subset. Choosing Z from source data does not alter this identity.

## 2. Failure on the declared positive record

The preceding five-vertex fixture has o with children u,C, u with leaves r,w, palette {a,b,c}, root support the full palette, and

    S_u=S_w={a,b}, S_C={c},
    S_r={a} in source zero, S_r={b} in source one.

Both preparations have profile (h_o,h_u)=(2,1). The same-union positive route for source one is -a(w), -a(u), ending at S_u={b}. Its positive memory projection is R=1[a absent at the still-existing u].

Under any uniformly applied ancestral pruning that retains u, S'_u remains {a,b}. Hence R remains zero in both source preparations. Removing u instead does not write this record: it removes the named output vertex and leaves the declared decoder without its required carrier. It is not an admitted positive endpoint for this task. The failure holds for every choice of Z, not just a symmetric or source-blind selection.

The successful same-union route changes only view a: it removes w and u from that view while the other views retain those vertices. Uniform pruning cannot remove a vertex from one view and keep it in another. That is the exact missing interaction in this attempted derivation.

## 3. What selective pruning would have to supply

The inherited v16.25 relation allows a family of individual retained subviews Z_i subset Y_i. Applying each view's own ancestral retraction gives those chosen Z_i. Requiring their union to remain T supplies the same-union guard. This is exactly the relation used in the preceding conditional theorem.

However, the family (Z_i) is an input to that comparison. The general retraction construction does not compute it from a physical source event. The source proof shows composition and monotonicity once the subviews are given. It does not establish which views lose which incidences during an interaction, or physically enforce preservation of their union.

A proposed physical realization therefore needs BOTH a justified indexed action, specifying how an actual event affects individual retained views, and the retention condition protecting the required carrier across that action. Calling the same global retraction once for each view with the SAME Z cannot provide this; calling it with different Z_i supplies the missing selective inputs.

The union condition is not cosmetic. It prevents deletion of the last support for a source witness. The following deliberately changed-carrier control shows why it cannot silently be inferred from the word pruning.

First uniformly prune the leaf r from the five-vertex tree: Z=T\{r}. This is a legal prefix retention. The two initially different view families become identical on the four-vertex carrier Z: S_u=S_w={a,b}, S_C={c}. Then, on that coarse carrier, selectively prune -a(w) and -a(u). Both original sources now yield the same positive memory S_u={b}.

At every state the current supports are nonempty and nested; the two remaining internal hitting numbers are (2,1). The coarse u is unary, which is permitted by the general prefix-view category but outside the old fixed binary/ternary carrier. This is not a counterexample to the previous fixed-T, same-union theorem: the first step violates precisely its fixed-union premise. Nor is this composite operation adopted as actual dynamics. It is an analytical control showing that ordinary common pruning can remove the protected witness, after which the otherwise legal selective update no longer certifies the original source.

## 4. Trace of the inspected event and source maps

The current source inputs are pinned in source_readbacks.json. This is an inspection of these concrete files, not a claim that the entire archive contains no other mechanism.

| v15.56 source_pushforward.py | J_c(v)=sum of J_f over the retraction fiber, forced by finite additivity of the supplied extensive grade | It transports amounts, not view membership; it does not specify (Z_i), initialize an incidence record, or make it accessible |

| v15.16 recoverability.py | Partial record pinching selected by an explicit four-bit mask on a supplied completed quantum encoding | That mask is neither derived nor an indexed lineage-retention family. Identifying its record bits with view labels would require an additional carrier/action connection |

The event-sufficiency result remains a valid exact conditional factorization; its failure to supply this interaction is not caused solely by the separate actual-outcome input. Even before outcome selection, the next instrument and its record dependence are supplied. Conversely, lack of deterministic outcome selection would not invalidate a genuinely derived interaction.

Likewise the extensive source channel can have a nontrivial source-dependent output after actual specified pruning. The source_binding.py and retained_amplitude.py inputs distinguish certified localization, relative retained grade and absolute observer normalization. Those existing conditional source constructions are preserved. They do not, in these files, identify extensive amounts with the selected incidence memory or supply an accessible physical readout of it. An amount-based consumer would require its own justified contract rather than being substituted for R after this candidate fails.

## 5. Scientific disposition and re-entry requirement

The candidate is stopped at a precise representational obstruction: uniform ancestral pruning cannot write a changed support at a surviving vertex. This is stronger than saying that the retained subset has not yet been selected; arbitrary selection of that subset does not fix the attempted map. The source trace locates the remaining supplied interaction inputs in the inspected alternatives.

Disposition: UNIFORM_PRUNING_INTERACTION_CANDIDATE_REJECTED; SELECTIVE_INTERACTION_AND_ACCESS_NOT_DERIVED.

The approved physical objective is NOT completed. No native force, physical record-acquisition law, actual successor law or retained observer access has been derived. No universal impossibility of interaction is claimed. The prior pruning-record theorem and its conditional positive example remain intact.

# Same-union pruning and protected incidence records

Date: 2026-10-11. Source parent: 95d0b2381f6006fb30c5fa7cd76ce80696bb3b2d.
Status: scoped analytical result ACCEPTED by separate review; see pruning_record_bridge/ANALYTICAL_REVIEW_RAW.md. No numerical campaign, physical mechanism or numbered-stage certification is claimed.

## Question and status of the restriction

The previous native-control boundary permits every reversible native incidence path inside a total-unit band. Ordinary writable controls cannot then certify an original source bit from a terminal state. This probe examines a different, already defined mathematical relation: same-union pruning of indexed retained views (v16.25 and v16.26).

We first identify its exact representation on the nested-support carrier. We do NOT infer that every native toggle is physically oriented this way, or that a physical system selects these refinements. Same-union pruning is an inherited allowed comparison, not an inherited law selecting actual successive states. Restricting the considered histories to it is an explicit conditional premise. The phrase 'time is pruning' does not supply a transition selector, force a deletion, or identify every abstract tree with physically accessible records.

The result below has three parts: an exact representation and reachability criterion; a pruning-protected conditional record with an initially identical memory; and a limit on erasing the original source distinctions while retaining a universally sound positive record. This is a separately typed mathematical consumer, not satisfaction of the C3 restored-marker gate or its swapped-root test.

## 1. Literal transposition of the same supplied incidence carrier

Let T be a fixed finite rooted tree, P a fixed finite nonempty indexed palette, and S a native support state: S_root=P, every S_v is nonempty, and S_child is a subset of S_parent. For each label i define

    Y_i = {v in T : i belongs to S_v}.

Every Y_i contains the root and is prefix closed. Nonemptiness of every S_v says precisely that the indexed views cover T. Conversely, a P-indexed family of root-containing prefix-closed subsets Y_i whose union is T defines S_v={i:v in Y_i}; this is nonempty, nested and has fixed root P. These maps are mutually inverse. Redundant or identical indexed views are allowed and remain distinct indices; root-only views are allowed.

At an internal v, a label set I intersects every immediate child support iff the views indexed by I jointly contain every immediate child. Thus the native hitting number h_v equals the inherited local child-cover number tau_v. This identifies the same labeled incidence data, not just equal dimensions or a fitted relabeling. All maps commute with transport of the fixed tree and view indices.

Deleting incidence (v,i), v nonroot, preserves nesting iff no child of v contains i; in a prefix-closed view this means v is a leaf of Y_i. It preserves support nonemptiness iff another view still contains v. Thus native single-incidence deletion is exactly atomic leaf pruning of one view with the same union T. This is v16.26's atomic refinement on the same supplied carrier. No new palette, vertex, metric or comparison target is introduced.

This is a mathematical representation equivalence. It does not construct the actual Genesis/source-record binding of a physical tree, make all labeled incidences observer-accessible, or transport extensive source amounts into a physical record. Those are distinct obligations.

## 2. Exact directed reachability from an exact preparation

For two support states E and S, write E<=S when E_v is a subset of S_v at every vertex. Fix a feasible target profile q=h(S) at every internal vertex and a nonnegative integer band budget B. Let

    D_q(F) = sum over internal v of |h_v(F)-q_v|.

Allow only native deletions, with every intermediate state satisfying D_q<=B. Zero-length paths are permitted. There is no compulsory completion or stopping rule.

**Endpoint criterion.** A native state E is reachable from S by such a path iff E<=S and D_q(E)<=B.

Necessity follows from deletion-only evolution and the endpoint band. For sufficiency, keep E fixed and repeatedly choose a deepest incidence to remove from F\E: equivalently, prune a leaf of some current Y_i\Z_i, where Z is the view representation of E. Prefix closure is preserved because no retained E descendant can lie below a vertex absent from E's corresponding view. Some E-view still contains each removed vertex because E covers T. Hence each step preserves nonemptiness and the union. Finite repetition reaches E, exactly as in v16.26 atomic factorization.

Shrinking child supports cannot decrease any h_v: a hitting set for the smaller supports also hits the larger ones. Therefore throughout this factorization

    q_v = h_v(S) <= h_v(F) <= h_v(E).

All deviations have the same nonnegative sign. Summing gives D_q(F)<=D_q(E)<=B. This proves the band condition at every primitive, not just at the endpoint. The argument works for every finite tree arity; it does not extend the reversible arity-2/3/4 normalization theorem, which is not used here. Its ingredients are inherited refinement monotonicity and atomic factorization.

There are exactly sum_v |S_v\E_v| actual edits on any deletion-only path from S to E, since no incidence can be reinserted. In particular exact-to-exact pruning paths stay exact throughout. Excursions cannot rise and then fall during pure pruning.

## 3. Exact criterion and cost for deleting a designated incidence

Fix a nonroot vertex v and a label a initially in S_v. Let Desc(v) include v. Form C by removing a from every support in Desc(v), leaving all other incidences unchanged. Nesting forces this entire removal whenever a is absent at v.

**Pruning-cone criterion.** Some band-admitted deletion path reaches a state with a absent at v iff:

1. No vertex u in Desc(v) has initial support S_u={a}; and
2. D_q(C)<=B.

The first condition makes C nonempty everywhere. Nesting and the fixed root are then preserved, since v is nonroot and all affected descendants lose the same label. If both conditions hold, the endpoint criterion reaches C. Conversely, any endpoint E with a absent at v satisfies E<=C by nesting. Such an E cannot exist with an initial singleton {a} anywhere below v. Otherwise coordinatewise hitting-number monotonicity yields D_q(C)<=D_q(E)<=B. This proves necessity as well.

When attainable, the minimum number of actual deletions to this first absence is

    m(v,a) = number of u in Desc(v) with a in S_u.

Every one of these incidences must be deleted, giving the lower bound. Delete them in descendant-before-ancestor order, with (v,a) last, to attain C in exactly m(v,a) moves. No other incidence is removed. This is a global minimum within the declared deletion-only class, not a minimum in the reversible native graph or a physical duration.

For two exact preparations with the same T,P,q and an initially present designated incidence in both, this supplies an exact sound-positive test: a nonvacuous positive record 'a absent at v' is universally sound for original source one iff this criterion holds for S_1 and fails for S_0. Positivity persists under every subsequent legal deletion because deleted incidences cannot return. This does not imply that any path actually reaches positivity.

## 4. Five-vertex conditional record, with no exclusive supplied script

Use P={a,b,c}, rooted tree o with children u,C, and u with leaves r,w. Fix the same reference identities and q_o=2, q_u=1 in both preparations. The source bit is represented by the supplied singleton at r; the proposed memory is the initially identical support at u.

| Vertex | Source zero | Source one |
|---|---|---|
| o | {a,b,c} | {a,b,c} |
| u | {a,b} | {a,b} |
| r | {a} | {b} |
| w | {a,b} | {a,b} |
| C | {c} | {c} |

Both preparations are nonempty and nested. At o, u and C are disjoint, giving h_o=2. At u, w intersects the singleton r, giving h_u=1. Use B=1, the same numerical total band as the preceding native-control discussion.

For source one, the path -a(w), then -a(u), keeps (h_o,h_u)=(2,1) at all three states. The cone endpoint has u=r=w={b}, C={c}. The record R=1[a absent at u] begins at zero and becomes one after two actual deletions. It remains one under every subsequent pruning history. Two is optimal in the declared deletion class because both (w,a) and (u,a) must disappear.

For source zero, r={a} cannot change under native deletion: deleting its only incidence would violate nonemptiness. Nesting therefore forces a to remain in u on EVERY deletion history, irrespective of ordering or other allowed changes. R can never become one. In the cone criterion, source zero fails its singleton condition and source one passes with D_q(C)=0.

The ordering needed for the successful pair follows from the native child-inclusion rule, not an externally supplied exclusive five-step script. All legal band-limited pruning paths are admitted, and arbitrary stopping is allowed. There are also unsuccessful paths: source one may first delete b(w), giving h_u=2 and w={a}; this remains inside B=1 but the surviving singleton at w then prevents a's deletion at u. No universal success, probability, fairness, actual outcome or automatic commitment follows.

The singleton source is protected here by nonemptiness AND the pruning-only premise. It is not an independently inserted immutable nonroot anchor within the reversible grammar. If additions are again admitted, it is mutable: source zero can take +b(r), -a(r), -a(w), -a(u), with all targets exact, and reach the same full positive endpoint. This explicit four-edit counterhistory reinstates the previous boundary. It is a hand-derived example, not a new numerical run.

The output R is a mathematical projection, not an earned observer read. The positive endpoint and both initial preparations have the same h profile, so those profile values alone do not read the record. The initial memory at u is common; the complete initial preparations differ at r. No physical readout, request resolution or source initialization has been derived. This is a persistent conditional record relation under actual same-union pruning, not a completed physical sensor.

## 5. Why pruning-only sound records cannot erase every original source distinction

Let S_0 and S_1 be arbitrary exact native preparations with common T,P,q, not necessarily comparable. Use the same budget B and the same endpoint readout R. By the endpoint criterion, a native band endpoint E is reachable from both exactly when E<=S_0 and E<=S_1.

Consequently, if E is reachable from S_1 but not from S_0, then E contains at least one incidence belonging initially to S_1 but not S_0. For if every incidence of E also belonged to S_0, E<=S_0 and the criterion would make it reachable from S_0. Thus every positive endpoint of a universally sound, nonvacuous source-one readout must retain at least one originally source-one-exclusive incidence at its ORIGINAL coordinate.

This is a necessary condition, not a sufficiency statement for any supplied projection. It applies even if all initial memory coordinates are identical and the reported memory is elsewhere: some original distinguishing incidence must still survive in the full state. Pruning cannot relocate all original source differences into initially common coordinates and then erase them all while preserving such universal historical soundness. A same-union endpoint that erases all those differences is also reachable from source zero.

The example retains (r,b), which was absent in source zero. It therefore respects this limit. It achieves persistence without source erasure. This differs from the five-edit conversion's source-erasing record, whose soundness depends on an exclusive protocol and whose route includes additions. The old conversion is not claimed achievable under pruning alone.

## 6. What has changed, and what is still supplied
